title: Jensen Ackles revisits Supernatural's original ending idea
body_md:
**Spoiler warning: This article discusses the series finale of Supernatural.**

More than six years after Supernatural ended, the fate of the Winchester brothers remains a subject of debate among viewers. Jensen Ackles, who played Dean Winchester throughout the show's fifteen seasons, has revisited an idea for the finale that could not be fully realized because of pandemic-era production restrictions. His recollection highlights how differently the farewell might have felt, even without necessarily changing the central outcome for its protagonists.

## The farewell that production restrictions prevented

According to a report on Ackles' remarks at a fan convention, the planned ending would have offered a wider reunion with familiar faces from the show's long history. It also would have involved a performance by Kansas, whose Carry On Wayward Son became an enduring musical association for generations of Supernatural viewers.

The significance of that idea goes beyond nostalgia. Over fifteen seasons, the series built an extensive supporting cast of friends, relatives and allies, many of whom disappeared from the story or died along the way. An opportunity to see more of those characters together would have acknowledged that the Winchesters' journey belonged to a community as well as to two brothers.

COVID-related restrictions made an elaborate gathering difficult to produce. The finale did retain one particularly meaningful return: Jim Beaver appeared again as Bobby Singer, the brothers' longtime surrogate father. That appearance offered a connection to earlier seasons, although the larger reunion Ackles recalled did not take place.

## Why the broadcast finale remains divisive

In the ending that audiences saw, Dean dies during a hunt. Sam lives out the rest of his life without his brother before the two ultimately reunite in heaven. For some viewers, the conclusion fittingly emphasizes the bond that sustained the series. Others have felt that such a long-running ensemble deserved a more expansive farewell.

The report's writer also argues that the preceding episode, which resolved the conflict with Chuck, felt more like a natural series conclusion. That is a critical opinion, not a universal verdict or a statement that Ackles rejected every element of the broadcast finale.

The alternative is best understood as a different emotional presentation of the ending rather than confirmation that the brothers' ultimate destinies would have changed. A wider reunion and the presence of Kansas might have given the final moments a stronger sense of collective closure.

Ackles' remarks do not announce a remake, a new episode or a revival. They instead offer a reminder of how extraordinary production circumstances shaped the farewell to one of television's longest-running supernatural dramas.

[Source report](https://www.cinemablend.com/television/supernatural-ending-jensen-ackles-actually-better-real-finale-complaints)
